body.html: Who Baanlugchange Hotel is for — the shortest way to put it: Baan Lugchang is a stay for people who come to Chanthaburi wanting a clean room, peace and quiet, a budget price, and the warm feeling of an owner looking after the place themselves, rather than chasing luxury, a pool, or big-hotel amenities · This isn't a Chao Lao–Khung Wiman beachfront resort, nor a downtown chain hotel you can walk from to the riverside community in a few steps · It's a small hotel of around 22 rooms set down a quiet lane in the Tha Chang area on the edge of Chanthaburi, run hands-on by the owners · Its charm is in well-kept simplicity — plenty of foreign reviews use the phrase "simple but smart clean rooms," meaning the rooms aren't fancy but are clean and cleverly laid out · The people it suits best are travellers driving themselves around Chanthaburi, couples wanting a quiet corner on a budget, travellers using Chanthaburi as a stopover before continuing to Trat or Koh Chang, and working travellers who just want a clean, quiet place to sleep at a fair price · Anyone wanting a hotel within walking distance of Nam Phu Market or the riverside community, a swimming pool, or in-house breakfast may find it isn't their match, because it's a small hotel on the edge of town that mainly sells quiet and value · Put simply, Baan Lugchang plays the "quiet, clean, owner who cares" angle very well at a price that's hard to find — but you have to come understanding that it's a small stay on the edge of town, not a full-service downtown hotel, and you should have a car or be ready to call a ride into town

Location and getting around — this is both a highlight and the thing to understand about Baan Lugchang · The hotel sits on Soi Raksakchamun 16, Tha Chang sub-district, Mueang Chanthaburi, a quiet residential area on the edge of town · The biggest plus is the quiet — plenty of real reviews agree it's a "quiet location on the outskirts," with restful, undisturbed sleep, ideal for people who genuinely want to relax · At the same time, the thing to know is that it isn't right in the centre — foreign reviews note you need a car or motorbike about 10 minutes into town to reach the main tourist areas like the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, Nam Phu Market, and the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception · The good news is many reviews praise how the owner is excellent at sorting out transport, giving suggestions, directions, and help calling a ride, so this isn't a big problem for anyone who plans ahead · For longer trips, Chanthaburi is about 245 km from Bangkok, roughly a 3.5–4 hour drive, with public buses from Ekkamai–Mo Chit into town · Anyone flying in lands at U-Tapao Airport (UTP) and drives on for about 1.5–2 hours · In short, if you have your own car this location works very well — quiet, easy parking, and an easy run into town or out to the sea · But if you don't have a car, plan your transport and ask the owner ahead of time, because the area has no dense public transport and isn't within walking distance of the sights

"It's very quiet and very clean here, the owner is kind and so helpful — both with calling a ride into town and recommending where to eat · The rooms are simple but well put together, and the morning coffee and snacks are nice · The only downside is there's no breakfast and you have to take a ten-minute ride into town, but at this price it's great value"

Room types and decor — Baan Lugchang has around 22 rooms in total, all air-conditioned, and from the booking platforms they break down into a few main types to choose from by group size and budget · The first is the King Bed Room, a single king for couples or solo travellers who want a big bed · The second is the Twin Room, two single beds for friends or colleagues who want separate beds · And the third is the Triple Room, with one single plus one queen, good for a small family or a group of three · The decor is simple and contemporary in an easy-on-the-eyes tone, focused on cleanliness and real usability over ornament, which matches the phrase foreign reviews use often — "simple but smart and clean" · Every room has the basics covered, with a flat-screen TV, fridge, air-con, free Wi-Fi, and en-suite bathroom plus basic amenities · A point many people like is that some rooms have a private balcony or lounge terrace looking out over the town or the hills in a peaceful setting, nice for a morning coffee or an evening wind-down · Real reviews agree the rooms are very clean and the beds comfortable, a key strength of a small owner-run hotel · To be straight about it, since it's a small 2-star hotel the rooms aren't spacious or resort-luxurious, and what's in them is just-enough rather than full of extras · The tip is to pick a room type by group size and to say in advance if you want a room with a balcony or a view, because not every room has them

Facilities and common areas — for a small 2-star hotel, Baan Lugchang covers the basics that budget travellers want, even without luxury extras · Start with what gets praised most often — free parking, which matters a lot for people driving around Chanthaburi, because there's plenty of space and no jostling like at a downtown hotel · There's free Wi-Fi in all rooms and common areas and a 24-hour front desk, which isn't common in a hotel this small and reassures anyone arriving late or leaving early · For services there's laundry, luggage storage, and a coffee/refreshments corner that many reviews mention positively as "coffee and refreshments good" · There's a lounge area and a common terrace where guests can sit out and catch the breeze in a quiet setting, and some rooms have a private balcony or patio looking over the town or hills · It has to be said plainly that there's no swimming pool, no fitness room, and no spa, and no lift, in keeping with the scale of a small hotel · The facilities are therefore simple, focused on cleanliness and basic convenience rather than completeness — but for quiet, cleanliness, and attentive care, it delivers fairly well above what you pay, and suits people looking for a place to "sleep well and genuinely rest" more than to use hotel amenities

Food and places nearby — the thing to understand from the start is that Baan Lugchang has no breakfast service and no hotel restaurant — foreign reviews state plainly "no breakfast facilities," which is worth knowing before you book · The offsetting plus is the hotel's coffee and refreshments corner, which many people say is good and helps you ease into the morning before heading out to find food · And honestly, coming to Chanthaburi you shouldn't be eating breakfast in the hotel in the first place, because Chanthaburi's food is a highlight of the trip · Just a roughly 10-minute drive into town gets you to Nam Phu Market, a well-known food spot with Chanthaburi rice noodles, mu chamuang (pork in chamuang leaf), local sweets, and seafood · Nearby is the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, with cafes, dessert shops, and long-standing riverside eateries · Around the Tha Chang area itself there are rice-and-curry shops, noodle shops, convenience stores, and small cafes to drop into · The owner also earns praise for recommending great spots and local food, which keeps first-time guests from getting lost over where to eat · Put simply, food isn't something to expect from the hotel itself, but a location just ten minutes from Chanthaburi's food and the owner's recommendations cover it easily, turning meals into a real part of exploring Chanthaburi rather than eating the same thing over and over at the hotel

Service and the owner — this is where Baan Lugchang earns the most consistent praise in real reviews, and the heart of why the overall score is high · Because it's a small hotel the owners run and look after closely, the service is very personal · Foreign reviews agree, writing "staff behaviour very good, very cooperative, always helpful" and noting the owner is "very helpful" with sorting out transport, calling a ride into town, and recommending sights and food · Many people feel they're being hosted like the owner's guest rather than just checking into a regular hotel — remembered by face, greeted warmly, and helped readily when something comes up · The 24-hour front desk also means guests arriving late or leaving early are looked after throughout · To be straight about it, since it's a small team the English may sometimes be basic, and the deluxe extra services of a big hotel naturally aren't there · But for sincerity, willingness to help, and attentive care, it's the clearest strength here, and the main reason many guests rate the service highly and say they'd come back

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling together Trip.com, Booking.com, Tripadvisor, and Expedia, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the most-mentioned things are the quiet and the cleanliness of the rooms, the owner and staff being friendly and more helpful than expected, great value for the budget price, convenient free parking, comfortable beds, a good coffee-and-snacks corner in the morning, and a relaxed edge-of-town setting that's genuinely good for resting · Many people call it a small hotel that's "reasonably priced" and "smart clean" to the point of feeling like more than what you paid · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned point is no breakfast (no breakfast facilities), so you head out to eat, being on the edge of town about 10 minutes from the tourist areas, needing a car or a ride into town, no swimming pool or resort-style amenities, simple rooms that aren't luxurious for a 2-star, and some feeling it's inconvenient for those without their own transport · Almost all the gripes are about setting expectations right and planning for transport rather than any issue with the quality of the stay — reflected in an overall score that's still high (8.9 on Trip.com) and the clearly consistent praise for cleanliness and the owner

"Booked it as a stopover before going on to Koh Chang, and ended up more impressed than I expected · The room was clean and so quiet I slept beautifully, and the owner helped with everything — directions and restaurant recommendations · No breakfast, but a ten-minute drive into town and you've got loads of Chanthaburi food, great value for the price"

Price and value — Baan Lugchang's price depends on the room type and the season, sitting overall in Chanthaburi's budget-stay group · Rooms start from around THB 700/night at normal rates, climbing to roughly THB 900–1,200 for a larger room like the Triple Room or over long weekends and high season · Compared with downtown Chanthaburi hotels like budget chains, where prices often start in a similar range but without this quiet and easy parking, and compared with what you get — a clean, quiet room, free parking, an attentive owner, and a location that gets you easily to both town and the sea — Baan Lugchang feels very good value among budget stays that sell quiet and cleanliness · The trade-off is accepting that it's a small hotel on the edge of town, with no breakfast, no pool, and the need for a car or a ride into town · For travellers driving themselves who value quiet and value over a central location, this is a deal that's hard to find at the price · But for those who want to walk to Nam Phu Market or the riverside community and need full amenities, the value here may be measured differently, and a downtown hotel is worth considering instead

Good to know before booking — a few things make the stay smoother · One, plan your transport well — it's on the edge of town about 10 minutes from the tourist areas, so if you're not driving yourself, ask the owner about arranging a ride or motorbike rental in advance, because the area has no dense public transport · Two, know that there's no breakfast — plan to head out for Chanthaburi food at Nam Phu Market or the riverside community, or use the hotel's coffee corner to start the morning first · Three, if you want a room with a balcony or hill view, say so when booking or ask the owner, because not every room has one · Four, check-in is from 14:00 (accepted until evening) and check-out is in the morning; if you're arriving late, give notice ahead, even though there's a 24-hour front desk · Five, use this as a base to explore Chanthaburi to the full — drive into town to see the riverside community and the cathedral, then the next day head out to the sea at Chao Lao–Khung Wiman beach or continue to Koh Chang/Trat with ease · Six, compare prices across platforms (Agoda / Booking / Trip.com) and pick free cancellation if your plans aren't set

The bottom line — from everything real reviews say, Baanlugchange Hotel, or Baan Lugchang, is the stay that suits best for people coming to Chanthaburi who want a clean, quiet room at a budget price, with an owner who looks after you like family · Being a small, owner-run hotel on the edge of town, with the cleanliness and quiet that reviews consistently praise, convenient free parking, and an affordable price, gives it a charm of its own that you won't find at a typical chain hotel — especially for people driving themselves around Chanthaburi, easy-going couples, and travellers using Chanthaburi as a stopover before continuing to the eastern sea · If you're after a hotel within walking distance of Nam Phu Market and the riverside community, with a pool, breakfast, and full resort-style amenities, this may not be the answer, and a downtown hotel or a beachfront resort is worth considering instead · But for a trip that wants a stay that's "quiet, clean, good value, and as warm as being hosted at the owner's home" — Baan Lugchang is the choice with heart, and the reason many guests write that they got more than they paid for and mean to come back next time they're in Chanthaburi

faq.q: Where is Baanlugchange Hotel · is it far into Chanthaburi town?
faq.a: The hotel is on Soi Raksakchamun 16, Tha Chang sub-district, Mueang Chanthaburi, a quiet residential area on the edge of town · It's about a 10-minute drive from central Chanthaburi, the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, and Nam Phu Market · It's not within walking distance of the sights, so a car is recommended, or ask the owner about arranging a ride in advance

faq.q: How much does Baanlugchange Hotel start at · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from around THB 700/night at normal rates · There's the King Bed Room (king bed), Twin Room (2 single beds), and Triple Room (1 single + 1 queen) for a small family · Larger rooms and high season cost more, so compare across platforms before booking

faq.q: Does Baanlugchange Hotel have breakfast and a swimming pool?
faq.a: No breakfast and no swimming pool · But there's a coffee and refreshments corner that real reviews praise as good · For food, the tip is to drive ten minutes into town for Chanthaburi food at Nam Phu Market and the riverside community — Chanthaburi noodles, mu chamuang, and local sweets

It suits people driving themselves around Chanthaburi, easy-going couples, and travellers using Chanthaburi as a stopover before continuing to Koh Chang/Trat who want a clean, quiet room at a budget price with an owner who cares · If you want to walk to Nam Phu Market and have a pool and breakfast, a hotel in town or a beachfront resort may suit better

faq.q: What are Baanlugchange Hotel's reviews and scores like?
faq.a: Scored 8.9 on Trip.com and around 8.4–8.7 on Expedia/Kayak from real reviews across multiple platforms · The most-praised points are the quiet, the cleanliness of the rooms, and an owner who's more helpful than expected · The main watch-outs are no breakfast, being on the edge of town, and needing your own transport to get around

faq.q: Can I stay at Baan Lugchang without my own car?
faq.a: Yes, but you need to plan — the Tha Chang area has no dense public transport and is about 10 minutes from the sights · The good news is the owner is good at arranging rides and advising on getting around · The tip is to ask in advance about a transfer or motorbike rental, or consider a hotel in town if you want to explore on foot
